programmes.name: Emergent Ventures
programmes.page_evidence: mercatus.org/emergent-ventures serves a live "Apply Now" button linking to https://mercatus.tfaforms.net/5099527. Page states "all applicants must be 13 years of age or older" and carries no deadline and no closure notice.
programmes.cash: Reported $1k-$100k, most awards around $50k (secondary sources; the Mercatus page itself discloses no range)

programmes.brand_value: High signal in the progress-studies and builder world; Tyler Cowen's imprimatur travels.
programmes.network_quality: Strong informal alumni network; the EV winners list is public.
programmes.notes: Best-fit row in this lane: rolling, global, no entity, individual-friendly, and the "zero to one, meaningfully improve society" framing maps onto a decision-forecast layer for software teams. Founder is in Bangalore, so the India vertical is reachable from the same form (separate row).

programmes.name: Emergent Ventures India
programmes.region: India (applicant may be anywhere; project must affect India)
programmes.page_evidence: Same live form as the main EV track. Mercatus page: "dedicated support available for projects with a focus on India, Africa and the Caribbean, or Ukraine"; applicants select India from the "My Project Will Affect" drop-down.

programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individuals; no team requirement
programmes.location_requirement: Project must have an India focus. No Indian entity required.

programmes.brand_value: Shruti Rajagopalan runs the India vertical; strong standing in the Indian builder ecosystem.
programmes.notes: Important: this is NOT a DPIIT-gated Indian government scheme, so the founder's ruling against incorporating an Indian entity does not bite. It is US philanthropic money with an India lens. Fit depends on framing Supaprod's India relevance; weaker than the general EV track on substance, but the same form, so near-zero marginal cost to select both.
